title: Pattern Headings: Wars
summary: Pattern list of free-floating subdivisions for individual wars (including coups, revolutions, uprisings, invasions, civil wars), whether established directly under their names or as subdivisions under place names. Wars entered under a place (e.g., United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865) may not take geographic subdivision after list subdivisions; wars entered directly may, with restrictions for single-jurisdiction wars. Governs --Participation, [...], bars --Participation, Foreign/[nationality] and --Foreign public opinion under the two world wars, and separates topical (sec. H) from form subdivisions (sec. I), the latter not used by LC since 2025 (LCGFT).
validation_rules: Subdivisions on this list are free-floating under headings for individual wars, whether entered directly under their names (e.g., `Crimean War, 1853-1856`) or as subdivisions under place names (e.g., `Turkey--History--Revolution, 1909`; `Transylvania (Romania)--History--Peasant Uprising, 1437-1438`; `Spain--History--Coup d'état, 1981`), including coups, revolutions, insurrections, uprisings, invasions, or civil wars, if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. (H 1200 secs. B, D)

Do not apply this list to individual battles (e.g., `El Alamein, Battle of, Egypt, 1942`; see H 1285), riots, demonstrations, protests, strikes, other unarmed disturbances, terrorist attacks, or headings using "war" metaphorically (e.g., `War on Terrorism, 2001-2009`). Exception: --Personal narratives and --Personal narratives with national or ethnic qualifiers may be used under headings for battles that are parts of wars. (H 1200 sec. C; sec. I)
Where a variant phrase or subdivision equivalent to a list subdivision is established in the subject authority file, the established variant takes precedence. (H 1200 sec. D)
A list subdivision marked (May Subd Geog) may be followed by a place only when the war is established directly under its own name, e.g., `World War, 1939-1945--Campaigns--France`. (H 1200 sec. F.1)

For a war established under its own name and fought in a single jurisdiction named or implied in the heading, add a place (per H 830) only to bring out a different place or a locality within that place, e.g., `Falkland Islands War--Military intelligence--Great Britain`; `South African War, 1899-1902--Campaigns--South Africa--Calvinia Region`. (H 1200 sec. F.1)
For a war established as a subdivision under a place name (e.g., `United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865`), do not further subdivide list subdivisions by place. (H 1200 sec. F.1)

Do not interpose a place between the war heading and a topical subdivision that does not subdivide by place; assign two headings instead, e.g., `World War, 1914-1918--Radar` and `World War, 1914-1918--Denmark` [not `World War, 1914-1918--Denmark--Radar`]. (H 1200 sec. F.1)

Use --Participation, [...] (e.g., `--Participation, Juvenile`) only for participation of a group in the military actions of a war; other aspects of the war in relation to a group use `[name of war]--[name of group]`, e.g., `World War, 1939-1945--Children`. (H 1200 sec. F.2)

--Participation, [nationality] covers direct participation of nationals in military actions (e.g., `Vietnam War, 1961-1975--Participation, Australian`) and foreign economic and technical assistance to combatants (e.g., `Poland--History--Revolution, 1863-1864--Participation, Swedish`). (H 1200 sec. F.2)
Do not use --Participation, [name of group] for the major combatants in any particular war. (H 1200 sec. F.2)

Do not use `--Participation, Foreign` or `--Participation, [nationality]` (e.g., `--Participation, German, [Irish, Swiss, etc.]`) under `World War, 1914-1918` or `World War, 1939-1945`; use `[name of war]--[country]`. (H 1200 sec. F.2; list)
Do not use `--Foreign public opinion` or `--Foreign public opinion, Austrian, [British, etc.]` under `World War, 1914-1918` or `World War, 1939-1945`. (H 1200 sec. H)

When assigning --Participation, [group of people or nationality], also assign a heading for the group (subdivided by place if appropriate) or for the country with an appropriate subdivision. (H 1200 sec. F.3.a)

For a subordinate jurisdiction in relation to a war established under a place, assign an additional heading for the subordinate jurisdiction, e.g., `Spain--History--Civil War, 1936-1939` and `Aragon (Spain)--History`. (H 1200 sec. F.3.b)

Exception for United States wars only: establish the war as an event under the locality, e.g., `Washington (D.C.)--History--Civil War, 1861-1865`; for a special topic, assign both `United States--History--Revolution, 1775-1783--Confiscations and contributions` and `New York (State)--History--Revolution, 1775-1783--Confiscations and contributions`. Do not apply this to any place other than the United States. (H 1200 sec. F.3.b)
`--Diplomatic history` is used only under wars established directly under their names; for wars under place names use `[country]--Foreign relations--[period]`. (H 1200 sec. H)
`--Reparations` is not subdivided geographically under individual wars. (H 1200 sec. H)

Subdivisions of the type `--Art and the war, [revolution, etc.]`, `--Education and the war, ...`, `--Literature and the war, ...`, `--Mass media and the war, ...`, `--Motion pictures and the war, ...`, `--Music and the war, ...`, `--Radio broadcasting and the war, ...`, `--Television and the war, ...`, `--Theater and the war, ...` must repeat the generic term for the engagement in the heading, e.g., `United States--History--Revolution, 1775-1783--Literature and the revolution`; `Sino-Vietnamese Conflict, 1979--Motion pictures and the conflict`; `Romania--History--Peasants' Uprising, 1907--Music and the uprising`. (H 1200 sec. H)
Do not use `--Songs and music--History and criticism`; use `--Music and the war, [revolution, etc.]` instead. (H 1200 secs. H, I)
`--Prisoners and prisons, British, [German, etc.]`: the nationality qualifier is the country controlling the prisons and holding the prisoners. (H 1200 sec. H)

`--Religious aspects` may be subdivided by a religion or Christian denomination: `[name of war]--Religious aspects--[name of religion or denomination]` or `[place]--History--[name of war]--Religious aspects--[name of religion or denomination]` (see H 1998). (H 1200 sec. H)

Class-of-persons subdivisions on the list (e.g., --Children, --Women, --Veterans, --Jews, --Refugees) may take further subdivisions from H 1100; --Law and legislation may take H 1154.5 subdivisions. (H 1200 sec. H)
`--Casualties--Statistics` (`$x Casualties $v Statistics`) is the form combination under individual wars; `$x Casualties` alone is topical (May Subd Geog). (H 1200 secs. H, I)

Form subdivisions valid under wars (sec. I): --Almanacs; --Art and the war, [revolution, etc.] (collections of art); --Autographs; --Biography; --Casualties--Statistics; --Chronology; --Gift books; --Pamphlets; --Personal narratives; --Personal narratives, American, [French, etc.]; --Personal narratives, Confederate; --Personal narratives, Jewish; --Pictorial works; --Portraits; --Registers; --Registers of dead (May Subd Geog); --Sermons; --Songs and music; --Songs and music--Texts; --Sources; --Treaties. (H 1200 sec. I)

Works about personal narratives use the topical forms `--Personal narratives--History and criticism`, `--Personal narratives, American, [French, etc.]--History and criticism`, `--Personal narratives, Jewish--History and criticism`. (H 1200 sec. H)

[LC practice] Since early 2025, LC catalogers do not assign the form subdivisions in sec. I; they assign LCGFT terms instead. The form subdivisions remain valid for other institutions. (H 1200 sec. I)

[LC practice] Establish new list subdivisions under `World War, 1939-1945` when possible, else under `United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865`, else under the specific heading needed. (H 1200 sec. G)
[LC practice] If an exceptional variant form is retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating form (H 195); otherwise propose changing the variant (H 193). (H 1200 sec. E)

sections.heading: A. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-03: Updated template. Clarified text. Separated general and form subdivisions. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: B. Types of headings covered
sections.text:
Headings for individual wars entered directly under their names or as subdivisions under place names. The category includes armed conflicts called by other names, such as coups, revolutions, insurrections, uprisings, invasions, or civil wars.

Examples:

```
Crimean War, 1853-1856
Turkey--History--Revolution, 1909
Transylvania (Romania)--History--Peasant Uprising, 1437-1438
Spain--History--Coup d'état, 1981
```

sections.heading: C. Types of headings not covered
sections.text: The category does not include individual battles of wars, for example, *El Alamein, Battle of, Egypt, 1942*. For instructions on individual battles, see H 1285. Also not included are riots, demonstrations, protests, strikes, or other unarmed disturbances, terrorist attacks, and headings that use the word "war" metaphorically rather than literally, such as *War on Terrorism, 2001-2009*.

sections.heading: D. Conflicts
sections.text: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

sections.heading: E. LC practice
sections.text: If an exceptional variant form is to be retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form following the procedures in H 195 if the reference does not yet exist. Otherwise, submit a proposal to change the variant form along with all bibliographic records requiring correction following the procedures in H 193.

sections.heading: F.1. Geographic subdivision
sections.text:
Subdivisions on this list with the notation (May Subd Geog) should be further subdivided by place only when used after a war established directly under its name, for example, *World War, 1939-1945*. For a war that is established under its own name and that was fought in a single jurisdiction that is either incorporated or implied in the name, further subdivide by place in accordance with H 830 only to bring out a place other than the one named or implied in the heading, for example, *Falkland Islands War--Military intelligence--Great Britain*, or to bring out a locality within that place, for example, *South African War, 1899-1902--Campaigns--South Africa--Calvinia Region*.

For a war established as a subdivision under the name of a place, generally a civil war or internal armed conflict, for example, *United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865*, the subdivisions on this list should not be further subdivided by place.

To bring out place in connection with topical subdivisions on this list which do not further subdivide by place, do not construct a single heading by interposing the place between the heading for the war and the topical subdivision. Instead, assign two headings: one for the war divided by topic and another for the war divided by place, for example, *World War, 1914-1918--Radar* and *World War, 1914-1918--Denmark*.

sections.heading: F.2. The subdivision --Participation, [...]
sections.text: Use subdivisions of the type --Participation, [...], for example, *--Participation, Juvenile*, for discussions of the participation of a particular group in the military actions of a war. Discussions of other aspects of a war in relation to a particular group, such as the war's effect on them, should be entered under a heading of the type [name of war]--[name of group], for example, *World War, 1939-1945--Children*. The subdivision --Participation, [nationality] should be used for works about direct participation of the nationals of the country in the military actions of the war, for example, *Vietnam War, 1961-1975--Participation, Australian*, as well as for works about foreign economic and technical assistance to the combatants, for example, *Poland--History--Revolution, 1863-1864--Participation, Swedish*. Do not use --Participation, [name of group] for the major combatants in any particular war. Do not use *--Participation, Foreign* or --Participation, [nationality] under the headings *World War, 1914-1918* or *World War, 1939-1945*. For the participation of a particular country in one of the world wars, use [name of war]--[country].

sections.heading: F.3. Additional headings for special topics
F.3.a. --Participation, [...]
sections.text: When assigning *--Participation, [group of people or nationality]*, assign in addition, either a heading for the group of people involved, subdivided by place if appropriate, or a heading for the country divided by an appropriate subdivision.

sections.heading: F.3.b. Topic and subordinate jurisdictions
sections.text:
For works discussing a subordinate jurisdiction in relation to a war established as a subdivision under a place, assign an additional heading for the subordinate jurisdiction, for example, *Spain--History--Civil War, 1936-1939* and *Aragon (Spain)--History*. However, for wars established as subdivisions under the heading *United States--History*, bring out a locality in connection with the war by establishing the war as an event under the locality, for example, *Washington (D.C.)--History--Civil War, 1861-1865*. For general works about the war in this locality, assign only the heading for the locality subdivided by the name of the war. For works about a special topic of a United States war in connection with a specific locality, however, assign both the general heading for the war with appropriate topical subdivision from the list below, as well as the heading for the locality subdivided by the name of the war and the same topical subdivision.

Example:

```
651 #0 $a United States $x History $y Revolution, 1775-1783 $x Confiscations and contributions.
651 #0 $a New York (State) $x History $y Revolution, 1775-1783 $x Confiscations and contributions.
```

Do not apply this exceptional practice for any place other than the United States (cf. H 1592, sec. 5.e.).

sections.heading: F.3.c. Other special topics
sections.text: In cases where a work discusses a specific aspect of a topic covered by a broader subdivision used under wars, assign an additional heading to bring out the specific aspect, if possible. For example, for a work on railroads of the South during the Civil War, assign both the headings *United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865--Transportation* and *Railroads--Southern States--History--19th century*.

sections.heading: G. New subdivisions
sections.text: Establish new subdivisions proposed for this list under *World War, 1939-1945* whenever possible. If a subdivision is not appropriate under that heading, establish it under *United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865*, if possible. If a subdivision cannot logically be established under either pattern heading, establish it under the specific heading required for the work being cataloged.

sections.heading: I. List of form subdivisions
sections.text:
LC practice: In early 2025, the use of form subdivisions was phased out. Library of Congress catalogers assign Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. Therefore, the form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by Library of Congress catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.
